rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 6 is the best raced design (score 56.87). It is iteration 0 with kd raised from 0.15 to 0.40, a clean single-factor change. Its oval progress rose from 0.1355 to 0.1575 and its s-bend progress from 0.1475 to 0.15, while slalom stayed at 0.105. Steering oscillation was flat (oval 0.1044 to 0.1047), so kd 0.4 showed no measurable noise cost. Every run so far has ended off track, and no run has finished.

What I kept, changed and rejected after the round-2 critique:
(1) Kept the single-factor step kd 0.40 to 0.80 from the raced iteration 6 design. Everything else is identical to iteration 6, so any score change is attributable to kd. This is the test the decision rule in my revision called for.
(2) Accepted that the noise claim was unchecked. I have not computed the derivative-noise path, so I do not claim kd 0.8 is safe. I rely on the measurement instead: steering_oscillation is reported per track, and I will judge it against each track's own baseline.
(3) Accepted that the 0.13 back-off threshold conflicts with the baselines (s-bend 0.1363 to 0.1382, slalom 0.1445 to 0.1467). The rule is now relative: back off kd only if oscillation rises more than 25% above that track's iteration 6 value (oval above about 0.13, s-bend above about 0.173, slalom above about 0.183).
(4) Accepted that the score gate of 56.87 has no margin against seed spread. The oval's per-trial spread is about 30 points. I judge the result on per-track progress first, and treat a three-track mean change under about 1 point as noise.
(5) Partly accepted the early-failure point. The s-bend progress has been near 0.15 across most settings, and this design does not test the start. I say so openly. A kd gain would not show that the robot can finish.
(6) Rejected the critique's suggestion of a lower speed. No evidence shows speed is the limit. I keep base_speed 1.5 and ki 0.05, so the test stays clean.
(7) Slalom is flat at 0.105 across all iterations. No lever here addresses it, and I make no claim that this change will move it.

Expected result: oval and/or s-bend progress above the iteration 6 values (0.1575 and 0.15), with steering_oscillation within the relative limit above and max_error still at about the 0.06 m limit. A three-track mean of about 56 to 60 is plausible, but the gain is uncertain.

Decision rules for the next revision: (a) If progress rises on at least two tracks and oscillation is within the relative limit, keep kd 0.8, and consider kd 1.2 alone. (b) If progress is unchanged within 0.01 on all tracks, damping is not the limit, and the next single test is base_speed alone (1.5 to 1.3 or 1.7). (c) If oscillation exceeds the relative limit on any track, or the mean score falls by more than 1 point, revert kd to 0.4. (d) If progress exceeds 0.9 with completion 0, raise base_speed by 0.1. (e) If line_loss_events exceeds 2 on any track, test search_right alone.
